chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: New Orleans musicians in Chicago: Guy Kelly, Natty Dominique, Punch Miller
summary: He worked with Guy Kelly and knew Punch Miller and Francois Mosely's Louisianians.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, did you know many of the New Orleans musicians that were in Chicago?
People from New Orleans were always pretty strange.
Yeah, right, well, see, I knew -- well, I worked with Guy Kelly.
Oh, man, he was a wonderful trumpet player.
Yeah, I have him some records with Jimmy Noon e.
Right, oh, yeah, right, right, right, right, right.
And Natty Dominique and then -- but he
wasn't the musician that Guy Kelly and -- what's his name that just died down in New Orleans not too long ago?

Punch Miller. Gee, I remember Punch when he was here, and we worked with Punch, and then Francois Mosely, I used to see him all the -- he had a band that called themselves the Louisianians. And he had a whole New Orleans band. Yeah. And almost all of the musicians from New Orleans -- we all mingled very close that year. So -- but they were very clannish, they stayed together. And they acted a little strange, like you said.
